name: @bitmuse/browser
description: A headless Chrome driven by Playwright, as tools that open pages, read them as an accessibility tree with element refs, click, type, fill forms, wait, run page JavaScript, take screenshots and inspect console, network, tabs and cookies, with one browser context per chat.

toolGroup.brief: Drive a headless Chrome with Playwright: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, click, type, fill forms, screenshot, inspect console and network.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Open a URL in this chat's headless browser (or go back, forward, reload) and get the page's accessibility snapshot: the tree of roles, names and `[ref=eN]` handles that every other browser_* tool addresses elements by. Normally the first browser call. A bare host like example.com means https. Each chat has its own cookies and storage; a helper chat shares its parent's by default. Reaches the network.

url.description: The URL to open. Required unless `action` is back, forward or reload.

waitUntil.description: When navigation counts as done. Default load; networkidle for a page that renders itself after load.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Re-read the current page as an accessibility snapshot with fresh `[ref=eN]` handles. Actions already return one, so use this when the page changed under you or your refs went stale (they do on every re-render). On a big page filter with `text` or `regex` instead of reading the whole tree.

text.description: Only lines containing this text, case-insensitive.

regex.description: Only lines matching this regular expression (case-insensitive unless given as /re/flags).

context.description: Lines of context around each match, like grep -C. Default 0.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element on the current page, addressed by a `[ref=eN]` from the latest snapshot, a selector, or x/y viewport coordinates as a last resort. Returns the page after the click, so a navigation it caused is visible. Refs belong to the snapshot that produced them.

target.description: The element: a ref like 'e7' from the latest snapshot (the reliable way), or a Playwright selector (CSS, 'text=Sign in', 'role=button[name="OK"]'). Omit only when giving x and y.

x.description: Viewport x, when there is no ref or selector.

modifiers.description: Keys to hold during the click.

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Move the mouse over an element to bring out what only appears under the pointer (a menu, a tooltip, a row's buttons), then return the snapshot.

target.description: The element: a ref like 'e7' from the latest snapshot (the reliable way), or a Playwright selector (CSS, 'text=Sign in', 'role=button[name="OK"]'). Omit only when giving x and y.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type into the page. `fill` (default) puts `text` into the field at `target`, replacing what was there; `press_key` sends one key or chord ('Enter', 'Tab', 'ArrowDown', 'Control+a') to `target` or the focused element; `fill_form` fills several fields in one call (much better than a call each); `select_option` picks `values` in a <select>. `submit` presses Enter after a fill. Returns the snapshot after.

target.description: The element: a ref like 'e7' from the latest snapshot (the reliable way), or a Playwright selector (CSS, 'text=Sign in', 'role=button[name="OK"]'). Needed by fill and select_option.

fields.description: For fill_form: the fields in order.

target.description: Ref or selector of the field.

value.description: What to put in it; for a checkbox or radio, true or false.

values.description: For select_option: the option values or labels.

slowly.description: Type key by key, firing the keystroke handlers an autocomplete needs.

tools.name: browser_wait
tools.description: Wait until text appears or disappears, an element reaches a state, or loading finishes, then return the snapshot. The action tools already wait for the page to settle; use this for a spinner, a toast, a slow request. Prefer a condition over a fixed `time`.

text.description: Wait until this text is visible.

textGone.description: Wait until this text is gone.

target.description: The element: a ref like 'e7' from the latest snapshot (the reliable way), or a Playwright selector (CSS, 'text=Sign in', 'role=button[name="OK"]').

state.description: The state `target` must reach. Default visible.

timeout.description: Give up after this many milliseconds. Default the extension's timeoutMs (15000).

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description: Run JavaScript in the page and get its JSON return value: the escape hatch for what the accessibility tree does not show (computed styles, scroll position, app state on window, extracting a table). An expression ('document.title') or a function ('() => [...document.links].map(a => a.href)'); with `target` the element is the function's argument. Return plain data, not DOM nodes; the result is cut at 8000 chars. It can change the page.

target.description: Optional element passed to the function: a ref or a selector.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Save the page (or one element, or the full scrolling page) as a JPEG or PNG, or print it to PDF with action 'pdf'. The file is written under `browser/` in your home and only its path comes back; open it from Files. JPEG quality 60 by default; ask for png for exact pixels.

action.description: Print to PDF instead of an image.

fullPage.description: The whole scrollable page, not the viewport.

type.description: Default jpeg, or png when filename ends in .png.

filename.description: The file's name. Default a timestamp.

format.description: PDF paper size, e.g. A4. Default Letter.

tools.name: browser_console
tools.description: Read the console messages and uncaught page errors since the last navigation, most recent last. The first place to look when a page is blank or broken.

level.description: This level or more severe. Default info.

limit.description: How many. Default 100 of the last 500 kept.

tools.name: browser_network
tools.description: List the requests the page made since the last navigation, numbered, with method, status and URL; `failedOnly` for the 4xx/5xx and connection failures, `filter` by URL regex, `index` for one request in full. Also lists requests this extension's host settings blocked.

index.description: One request in full, numbered as in the list (from 1).

filter.description: Only URLs or statuses matching this regex, case-insensitive.

failedOnly.description: Only failures and status 400 and above.

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: List this chat's tabs (the active one marked *), or open, switch to or close one. Every other browser tool acts on the active tab. A link that opens a new tab shows up here.

index.description: The tab, zero-based. Needed by select; close defaults to the active tab.

url.description: For new: open this URL in it.

tools.name: browser_state
tools.description: Read or change the browser's own state rather than the page's: cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, the whole storageState, dialogs, and the viewport size. Dialogs (alert, confirm, prompt) are dismissed automatically; to accept one, call kind 'dialog' action 'accept' BEFORE the click that opens it. Resize with kind 'viewport' to check a responsive layout.

action.description: Default list. accept and dismiss are for dialog.

name.description: The cookie name or storage key.

domain.description: Cookie domain for set. Default the page's host.

promptText.description: What to answer a window.prompt with, when accepting.

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description: Close this chat's browser, discarding its tabs, cookies and storage. Rarely needed (idle browsers close themselves); use it to start a login from a clean state or to recover from a wedged page.

tools.name: browser_status
tools.description: Show whether the headless browser is running, which Chrome and Playwright it uses, this chat's tabs, and the settings in force. Starts nothing; 'not running' before the first navigation is normal.

executablePath.help: Chrome or Chromium to drive. Empty: /usr/bin/google-chrome, chromium and the like are tried, then Playwright's own download.

headless.help: Run without a window. Leave on unless the host has a display.

timeoutMs.help: How long one action or navigation may take, in milliseconds (1000-300000).

idleMinutes.help: Close a chat's browser context after this many idle minutes; the browser itself stops when none is left.

viewportWidth.help: Viewport width in pixels for new contexts.

viewportHeight.help: Viewport height in pixels for new contexts.

snapshotChars.help: The most characters of accessibility snapshot one result carries before it is cut with a note.

valueChars.help: The most characters of a browser_evaluate result or a storage value.

screenshotDir.help: Where screenshots and PDFs are written, relative to home.

shareWithSubagents.help: A helper chat uses its parent chat's browser (tabs, cookies, logins). Off: each helper chat gets its own.

allowHosts.help: If set, pages may only be opened on these hosts: comma-separated, `example.com` includes subdomains, `*.example.com` only subdomains.

denyHosts.help: Hosts pages may never be opened on, same form as allowHosts.

blockPrivateNetworks.help: Refuse every request (pages and their resources) to loopback and private addresses: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8, link-local, fc00::/7.
